title: E2E metering validation harness for mixed sync/async clients and retry semantics
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: We have recurring production anomalies where token credits are inconsistent across REST and streaming clients under mixed load and retry patterns. Existing tickets focus on reconciliation and fragment attribution, but we lack a repeatable, end-to-end validation harness that can exercise sync (REST), async (websocket/streaming), and hybrid client behaviors together with realistic retry/backoff and partial-response cases.

Goal: Build a deterministic, configurable E2E metering validation harness that: (1) replays synthetic client mixes against local and staging metering pipelines, (2) asserts per-session input/output token attribution matches expected accounting, and (3) surfaces non-deterministic credits caused by reorders, retries, and partial deliveries. The harness should be usable by infra, runtime, and SRE teams to validate fixes and guard regressions.

Scope: Include test drivers for REST single-shot requests, streaming websocket clients with fragmented frames, and a proxy that can inject reorder/delay/duplicate frames. Track session IDs, request IDs, and eventual token tallies as produced by the metering pipeline. Support recording mode (capture real traffic sample) and synthetic mode (configurable patterns).

Success criteria: (A) Harness runs deterministically on CI with seeded RNGs and reproduces a known historical discrepancy from production; (B) Test suite includes at least 12 scenario permutations (mix ratios, retry strategies, out-of-order fragments, midstream model switch); (C) CI job fails if any per-session accounting delta > 0.5% across 1000 sessions; (D) Documentation and on-call runbook completed.

Acceptance constraints: Must not require production keys or access to customer data. Use sanitized traces or synthetic inputs. Run time for CI job should be <= 30m for full suite; we will provide a fast smoke subset for PRs.

Notes: This is a testing/validation effort, not a production fix. Findings should feed into follow-up tickets for pipeline fixes, rate limiter adjustments, or SDK changes.
reproduction_steps: 1) Run harness in synthetic mode with seed=12345 and client_mix=50/50 REST/streaming
2) Configure proxy to simulate 10% frame duplication and 5% reorder windows up to 2s
3) Start metering pipeline pointing at staging metering ingestion and the local validator sink
4) Assert per-session input/output token totals equal expected tallies and that no session shows final-credit drift > 0.5%
5) Switch to recording mode to capture a short production sampling (sanitized) and replay locally
proposed_solution: Implement a lightweight harness in Go (shared infra language) with pluggable client drivers. Harness will instrument session lifecycle (session start, fragments, finalization), compute a ground-truth token tally via the same tokenizer library the runtime uses, and compare against metering pipeline outputs pulled from the staging metering sink. Provide CLI flags for fault injection (delay/dup/reorder/drop) and a CI job that runs the canonical scenario matrix. Add metrics export (Prometheus) and verbose trace logs (structured) for triage.
risks: False positives if tokenizer versions drift between harness and runtime — lock tokenizer dependency or vendor a copy
CI runtime could be flaky if network fault injection is nondeterministic — ensure seeds and deterministic scheduling where possible
Privacy risk if recording mode accidentally captures PII — enforce sanitization and manual approval before replaying any recorded sample
qa_plan: Create smoke CI job with 3 fast scenarios (REST-only, stream-only, mixed small payloads)
Run full suite nightly against staging for one week and compare deltas with baseline
On failure, collect harness traces, metering sink exports, and open an investigation ticket with 'harness-evidence' label
